newsitem.title: FRANCE: ETA planned to kidnap or kill Princess Elena - report.
newsitem.headline: ETA planned to kidnap or kill Princess Elena - report.

text.p: The Basque separatist group ETA planned to kidnap or murder Spanish King Juan Carlos's daughter Elena at one of her riding schools in south-west France, a French counter-terrorism expert said on Monday.

Roland Jacquard, president of the International Observatory on Terrorism, told the daily France-Soir in an interview that investigators had found documents linking suspected ETA leader Jose Luis Urrosolo Sistiaga, arrested last month, to the plan.
"Urrosolo had planned a very media-friendly, symbolic coup: the kidnapping or assassination of the Spanish infanta Elena," said Jacquard, who has close links to French security sources.
French police were not immediately available for comment.

"Documents found at the time of his arrest show that he had carried out very precise surveillance of the locations where the daughter of the Spanish King trained in horse-jumping at clubs in south-west France," Jacquard said.
French police arrested Urrusolo, armed with a handgun and carrying false identity papers, on January 16 after he drove through a police barrier in Bordeaux in the south-west.
Urrusolo, suspected of being one of ETA's three top members, had planned to kill a French military officer in Bordeaux on January 19, the Spanish daily El Mundo reported on Sunday.
If accurate, it would have been the first murder of a French target carried out by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) in France.

Spanish officials say ETA may be turning to French targets because of the increased cooperation between Spain and France in the fight against the separatist group. Such cooperation has led to more than 200 arrests in the past decade.
ETA has killed some 800 people since 1968 in its violent campaign for an independent state.
